rule.order: the 40 states are built by the plan phase in this fixed order: stratum t03_carry_over (6, as listed), then dev_proximate (seed 1000..1019), then train_proximate (seed 3000..3004), then fixed_grid (seed 1000,1001,1002 x 400,800,1200); indices 0..39 are assigned in that order
rule.floor: every state frame is floored to the 2-frame decision grid (floor_to_2)
rule.dedup: no two states of this pilot share (seed, decision_frame); the strata are constructed to be disjoint and the plan phase refuses a duplicate instead of silently dropping one
rule.fallback: if a seed has no first death within probe.max_frames, or the floored proximate frame would be < 40, that seed's proximate state is replaced by the fixed-grid frame 1200 floored and clamped to the last decision of its recorded trace (needs >= 40 frames of prefix); the replacement is recorded per state as fallback_used = true with the reason
rule.uniqueness_note: the fallback is the only branch in the rule; it is decided by data (does the A0 probe die before 6000 frames) but its form is fixed here, before any arm runs
rule.no_reselection: after states_frozen.json is written the state list is never edited; a shard that fails is rerun on the same frozen list

t03_carry_over.definition: the six states T03s reported as having both a death and a survival among the arms it measured (evidence/T03/student_continuation.json §5.2), kept verbatim: (seed 10, frame 1448), (seed 11, frame 1716), (seed 11, frame 1760), (seed 11, frame 1896), (seed 12, frame 1704), (seed 12, frame 1736)
t03_carry_over.why: the task requires the six already-known discriminating states to be part of the pilot; keeping them also pins a bridge to the previous round's verdicts
t03_carry_over.trace_note: read-only T03 traces (the frozen 20k student's own recorded trajectory). The prefix is policy-independent: it is the recorded per-frame mask sequence of the same RESET, so A0 can continue from these states and the expected HASH is the trace's own.

dev_proximate.definition: one state per dev seed 1000..1019; for seed 1000+i the offset is offset_grid[i % 8]; the state frame is floor_to_2(first_death_frame(seed) - offset)
dev_proximate.why: the rule A1 would actually use: pre-death proximate states on the development split, with the offset rotating over the whole 0.5-5 s window so the pilot measures the offset dependence of discrimination instead of one arbitrary offset

train_proximate.definition: one state per train seed 3000..3004; for seed 3000+j the offset is offset_grid[j]; the state frame is floor_to_2(first_death_frame(seed) - offset)
train_proximate.why: fresh, never-before-used train ancestors (the D410-S1 corpus only has seeds 10/11/12). G420-1 also needs >= 10 distinct training ancestors, so these seeds are the cheapest way to grow that denominator without touching dev or confirm

fixed_grid.definition: dev seeds 1000, 1001, 1002 x frames 400, 800, 1200 (each floored to the 2-frame decision grid)
fixed_grid.why: the control stratum: normal, far-from-death states at fixed episode frames. It measures the base rate of discrimination away from the death window, so a low overall rate can be read as 'the sampling rule, not the machinery, decides feasibility'.

unknown.handling: fail-closed: an unknown arm is never a survival and never a death; it is excluded from |S| and disqualifies its state from the discriminating count

definition.|S|: candidates whose verdict is engine_alive/executed; unknown and engine_death are never members (contracts.safe_action_set)

discriminating.definition: a state is discriminating when 0 < |S| < 18 and every one of its 18 arms carries a valid verdict (fail-closed: any unknown arm disqualifies the state from this count)

wall.note: every wall clock here is a value observed on a shared 20-vCPU host while other work was running: it is a contention-observed measurement, not a throughput promise

extrapolation_200x18.arithmetic: 3600 arms x the measured per-arm wall clock; this is an arithmetic extrapolation of one measured distribution, NOT a commitment, and it excludes per-command interpreter/engine startup and any queueing a real schedule would add

verdict.statement: the pre-registered rule (>= 5% discriminating and >= 2 non-empty |S| buckets) is MET

cross_check.note: summarise_contrast is the round's own summariser; it counts a state with an unknown arm as proper_18 because it only checks 0 < |S| < 18 and the arm count. This pilot therefore reports its fail-closed discriminating rate separately and never uses proper_18 as the A1 rate.

g420_1.reason: this is the frozen-student continuation contrast (WP420-02 §5's second leg) on a 20+ state slice, not the 200-state full-candidate pass; the gate is unchanged by it
g420_1.informative_definition: 0 < |safe set| < arms tested, i.e. among this round's 2-4 first actions at least one died and at least one survived; this is the quantity the teacher-continuation round measured as 0 of 20

missing.requirement: 50 failure-related states with a frozen-student continuation contrast
100 informative states; this round's informative definition is 'a death and a survival among the tested arms'

notes: every arm is RESET -> HASH-checked prefix replay -> candidate 2 frames -> the frozen A0 student's own 2-frame closed loop, capped at H=120
the safe set is computed only by contracts.safe_action_set
the |S| histogram and the discriminating rate are computed here; the cross_check block proves they agree with counterfactual.summarise_contrast
